purpose: Oxazepam is used to help relieve anxiety, nervousness, and tension. It is also used to help manage anxiety related to depression and to help with alcohol withdrawal symptoms. It works best for short-term use while you and your doctor work on the bigger picture of your mental health.
how_it_works: Your brain has a natural calming chemical called GABA. Oxazepam boosts the effect of GABA, which slows down overactive brain activity that causes anxiety. Think of it like turning down the volume on a nervous system that is working overtime, helping you feel calmer and more relaxed.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness and feeling sleepy are the most common effects. You may also feel dizzy, unsteady on your feet, or a little confused, especially when you first start taking it. Some people feel sluggish or have a mild headache. These effects are usually worse at the beginning and tend to improve over time.
warnings: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication — it can cause dangerous drowsiness and slow your breathing. This medicine can be habit-forming, so only take it exactly as prescribed and do not stop it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as that can cause withdrawal symptoms. It is not safe to drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have liver, kidney, or breathing problems before taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 10 to 30 mg taken by mouth, 3 to 4 times a day, depending on what it is being used for. Your doctor will start you on a lower dose and adjust it based on how you respond. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribes and never take more than directed.
